Let \(p=2027\) and \(m=\frac{p-1}{2}=1013\).

For \(k>m\), the binomial coefficient \(\binom{2k}{k}\) is divisible by \(p\), so

\[
S\equiv \sum_{k=0}^{m} k\binom{2k}{k}2^k \pmod p.
\]

For \(0\le k\le m\), one has the congruence

\[
\binom{2k}{k}\equiv (-4)^k\binom{m}{k}\pmod p.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{k=0}^{m}\binom{2k}{k}x^k
\equiv \sum_{k=0}^{m}\binom{m}{k}(-4x)^k
=(1-4x)^m \pmod p.
\]

Therefore

\[
S\equiv 2\frac{d}{dx}(1-4x)^m\bigg|_{x=2}.
\]

Now

\[
\frac{d}{dx}(1-4x)^m=-4m(1-4x)^{m-1},
\]

so

\[
S\equiv -8m(1-8)^{m-1}
\equiv -8m(-7)^{m-1}\pmod p.
\]

Since \(-8m=-4(p-1)\equiv 4\pmod p\),

\[
S\equiv 4(-7)^{1012}\pmod{2027}.
\]

By Euler’s criterion,

\[
(-7)^{1013}\equiv \left(\frac{-7}{2027}\right).
\]

Now

\[
\left(\frac{-1}{2027}\right)=-1,\qquad
\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)=-1,
\]

so

\[
\left(\frac{-7}{2027}\right)=1.
\]

Hence \((-7)^{1013}\equiv 1\), giving

\[
(-7)^{1012}\equiv (-7)^{-1}\equiv -\frac17.
\]

Thus

\[
S\equiv 4\left(-\frac17\right)=-\frac47\pmod{2027}.
\]

Since

\[
7\cdot 289=2023\equiv -4\pmod{2027},
\]

we get

\[
-\frac47\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
